title: Multiple Meat Sandwich on White Bread

content.title: About
content.content: The Multiple Meat Sandwich on White Bread (1855) is a hearty sandwich made with thin slices of beef, ham, chicken breast, and sausage layered between two slices of soft white bread. It is typically served with lettuce, tomato, and a light sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original 1855 recipe used only three meats: beef, ham, and chicken.
White bread in this sandwich is traditionally baked without seeds to let the meat flavors shine.
The sandwich is a common quick lunch option in school cafeterias.
Some regions add a slice of smoked bacon for extra aroma.
The product name comes from the menu code 1855 used by a large café chain.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Multiple meat types provide essential amino acids for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and chicken breast are rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Balanced carbohydrates
items.content: White bread offers a quick source of glucose for immediate energy.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Added lettuce and tomato increase dietary fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats like ham and sausage can be salty, which may affect people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Certain meats, especially sausage, contain saturated fats that should be limited.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific meat proteins.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: White bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. Serve with mustard, mayo, or a light yogurt sauce. For a fresher taste, add cucumber, radish, or extra lettuce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the components: store meat in an airtight container, keep bread in a dry place, and keep vegetables in a separate bag.
